title: Reading: the binding period as an involution statistic and the shape of its kernel
html:
Remark. Reading: the binding period as an involution statistic and the shape of its kernel

The balanced dimension sum S^{\mathrm{bal}}(n; q) is the fibre-level numerator of the classical binding period: at q = 1 it specialises to the involution count I(n), and the body-order period is I(n)/n (prop:sw-period-residue-sum). The identity of prop:binding-period-involution-statistic therefore locates the open recurrence kernel R(q, x) of prop:binding-genfun-qdifference at the level of a permutation statistic: the binding period is the generating function of involutions by 2\,\mathrm{maj} + \mathrm{content} \circ \mathrm{RSK} — a different statistic from the crossing statistic of the q-Hermite family.

Two structural consequences follow, both verified exactly.

  1. The kernel is an insertion recursion, not a finite q-difference operator. Splitting the involutions by the fate of the largest letter, the fixed-point-insertion weight ratio is non-monomial with growing polynomial spread, so the statistic is not Markovian under RSK insertion on any fixed finite basis (computations/lever1-kernel-maj-involution-identification.witness.json).

  2. The exact kernel object is a descent-set transfer operator. The statistic is Markovian on the lifted state space of pairs (shape, marked corner row): the level-k step factorises as T_k = A_k + q^{2k} B_k, where the non-descent block A and the descent block B carry only the monomial entries q^{c} with c the content of the added cell, the sole level dependence being the scalar q^{2k} on B. The operator reconstructs the right-hand side exactly, while its state space grows without bound (like the corner-marked Young lattice), so no fixed-depth q-difference projection closes (computations/lever1-descent-transfer-operator.witness.json).
